item: A dead Wikipedia stream is restarted, Start and Run-now resume the lane, the drain loop keeps trying, and the soak window says why a lane is quiet
status: shipped (fixture-verified; awaiting the operator's next bundle)
key_paths: src/wiki/runner.py; src/wiki/service.py; src/monitoring/release_run.py; src/api/scheduler.py; src/monitoring/soak_window.py; tests/test_wiki_lane_supervisor.py; tests/test_wiki_runner.py; tests/test_wiki_drain_bound.py; tests/test_wiki_counters.py; tests/test_wiki_online_resume.py
summary: Read from the 15 diagnostics bundles of 2026-10-06: two lanes were quiet for days (hP from 10-04 08:07, NUC for 116 hours with its lane halted) and the bundles carried no service state to say why; reading the code found two ways a lane can stay dead. The stream thread ended for good on a refused reconnect with nothing to start it again, and the drain loop ended for good after 3 failed drains. revive_stream restarts a dead stream before each drain (under a lock shared with start and stop); start_wiki_lane revives or rebuilds the lane, also when the stream is alive over a dead drain loop, and is now also called by /api/scheduler/start and /run-now (R117: only a lane whose setting says running); failed drains wait 30 s growing to a 300 s ceiling (FAILING_RETRY_CEILING_S, which protects how long a recovered lane sits idle and how long the single writer is left alone), the exponent capped so the wait cannot overflow, and the status reports degraded, retry_in_s, retry_due_at, the last error and its time, why the stream last ended and a failed restart; stop_wiki_lane joins outside the status lock but under a stop lock a start takes first; the idle sleep is sliced so a stop is noticed within a second; the soak-window lane block carries the service state (also when there is no lane file or it cannot be read), with the setting and the kill switch, and a zero-byte lane file reads as never stored anything. 34 new tests and 6 updated, mutation-checked.
